newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam blasts foreign media over labour campaign.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam blasts foreign media over labour campaign.

text.p: Vietnam took international broadcasters to task on Thursday over their coverage of Hanoi's plans to involve millions of people in a compulsory labour programme, describing their reports as slanderous.

The official Vietnam News Agency carried a commentary, also published in the Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper, blasting U.S. network Voice of America and the British Broadcasting Corporation for alleged distortions of government policy.
It said the two broadcasters had claimed the policy was one of forced labour, and accused them of "a gross interference in the internal affairs of an independent state..."
"It is quite wrong to spread those slanderous reports in an attempt to incite the Vietnamese people and break their national unity," the commentary said.
"These allegations are also insults by people who claim they have the right to teach others but who have little knowledge about history and social traditions thousands of years old."
Hanoi has had a compulsory labour programme for many years under which young people are required to contribute 10 days' work each year for free or pay an exemption fee.

Earlier this month the government announced plans to breathe new life into the programme by expanding the age group of participants and allowing individual provincial or city authorities to set their own exemption fees.

According to government officials the plan will involve the mobilisation of millions of people for involvement in both small and large infrastructure projects, thereby reducing rural under-employment and stemming migration to cities.
Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet was quoted by domestic media as saying one such project was an ambitious $5.5 billion north-south expressway running along stretches of the wartime Ho Chi Minh trail.
The trail was used by Hanoi to funnel supplies in their fight against U.S.-backed forces of what was then South Vietnam.
The Nhan Dan commentary described the task as a normal, internal affair and said reports to the contrary were aimed at inciting the Vietnamese people and breaking national unity.
